Mechanically FALSE: handle_input (main.odin:452) runs AFTER the frame's step/hash, so the append sits below the NEXT step's events_before mark (main.odin:358) and is excluded from every [events_before:] slice, while replay's command-loop emission lands inside its apply-tick slice; tick_events bytes feed state_hash (core/serialize.odin). The codebase's own parity.odin:202-208 note states the correct mechanics ('a dispatch-time event would land before the hash mark and never ride the pinned stream'). r1's acceptable remedy was to document the EXCLUSION honestly; the shipped comment asserts its opposite. Corroborated by architecture + codebase lenses.

findings.title: still present since round 1 — "ALL FOUR kinds" claim for audio.dem remains in the PR body (W1 reworded run.odin + audio.dem but not _pr_body.md:17)
findings.evidence: _pr_body.md:17: "`audio.dem` now proves ALL FOUR kinds fire (wire via its 100 ms draws)"; demos/audio.dem:19: "# so the consumer exercises THREE kinds in this golden"; harness/run.odin: "NO growth on, so NODE_SPAWNED cannot fire here — spawn lives in audio_spawn.dem".

findings.title: still present since round 1 — the W5 'byte-identical slices, live vs replay' comment is mechanically false (the fast-path event is excluded from every per-tick hash slice)
findings.evidence: main.odin:358 events_before := len(app.state.events) at step start; :367 step(&app.state, app.tick, {}, &cat); :390 h := state_hash(..., events[events_before:], ...); :452 handle_input (commit_draw's append) runs AFTER the hash; core/serialize.odin folds tick_events into the hash; harness/parity.odin:202-208: 'a dispatch-time event would land before the hash mark and never ride the pinned stream anyway'.
findings.detail: The fix's chosen remedy (document) was r1-acceptable, but the comment asserts identity instead of the exclusion: the append sits below the next step's mark, replay's emission sits inside its slice — app per-tick sim_hash diverges at draw ticks (diagnostics-only; no gate compares it).
findings.recommended_fix: Correct the comment to document the exclusion (live stats/overlay stream omits PIPE_DRAWN at draw ticks; the event rides the audio consumer's audio_mark slice only) — or emit inside the hashed window if equality is actually wanted.

findings.title: Wire/spawn play+mute paths (audio_flush play loops, toggle_mute stop loops) have zero automated coverage; the guards pin draws only
findings.evidence: audio.odin:306-313 PlaySound loops; :326-329 four StopSound loops; grep toggle_mute|audio_flush in *_test.odin: no matches; harness/run.odin guards assert *_draws < 1 only (draws, never plays/mute).
findings.detail: The device-gated half of the two new families is behavior change with no executable test (consistent with the 7.2 convention, but each new family widens the surface; the header's 'consumer mirror' mitigation covers the pure half only). P2.
findings.recommended_fix: Extract the variant-cycle computation into a pure helper and pin it; add a device-off flush test (pending clears on mute); keep rl calls manual-verified.

findings.title: Wire placeholder comment says the thump sits 'under' the tock — it is appended after it (sequential, the W2 class)
findings.evidence: :439 '// the confirm "tock": a low-mid falling sweep + a low thump under it'; :445-446 click_append(..., 0.055, 0.6) then tone_append(thumps[slot], 0.05, 0.45) — tone_append is append-only, so the thump occupies 55-105 ms AFTER the tock.
findings.detail: Only the comment is wrong (105 ms total is inside the README's <=120 ms wire envelope; the sound itself is fine). Same wording class r1's W2 fixed for spawn ('MIXED ... not three sequential').
findings.recommended_fix: Reword to 'followed by a low thump', or mix the two layers in one window (chime_append-style) if layering is intended.
